ladders.title: Magnetic field records
ladders.intro: The strongest field made by each kind of magnet, from steady superconducting magnets to explosive flux compression, which destroys the experiment.

rows.description: All-superconducting user magnet (LTS outsert + REBCO insert), NHMFL
rows.citation: National High Magnetic Field Laboratory news release, 12 Dec 2017: 32 T reached on 8 Dec 2017.

rows.description: All-superconducting user magnet, 35 mm usable aperture, CAS SECUF (Beijing)
rows.citation: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, release on the Synergetic Extreme Condition User Facility: 35.6 T with a usable aperture of 35 mm on 24 Jan 2026 (built with the Institute of Electrical Engineering, CAS).
rows.note: Institutional announcement. Record for all-superconducting user magnets; between it and the 32 T NHMFL magnet lie 32.35 T (Institute of Electrical Engineering, CAS, announced Dec 2019) and 35.1 T (Institute of Plasma Physics, Hefei, announced Sep 2025).

rows.description: All-resistive DC magnet, CHMFL Hefei (32.3 MW)
rows.citation: Hefei Institutes of Physical Science, CAS, release: 42.02 T on 22 Sep 2024 at 32.3 MW.

rows.description: Hybrid DC magnet (superconducting outsert + resistive insert), CHMFL
rows.citation: Chinese Academy of Sciences release, 15 Aug 2022: 45.22 T on 12 Aug 2022 in a 32 mm bore.

rows.description: REBCO test coil (14.4 T) operated inside a 31.1 T resistive background, NHMFL
rows.citation: Hahn et al., Nature 570, 496-499 (2019).
rows.note: The peer-reviewed record; DC, small test coil. Exceeded in 2025 (see lbc9_48p7t).

rows.description: REBCO test coil (Little Big Coil 9) operated inside a 31 T resistive background, NHMFL
rows.citation: National High Magnetic Field Laboratory news release, 11 Sep 2025, and research highlight, Jan 2026: 48.7 T in August 2025, the test coil adding 17.6-17.7 T to a 31 T resistive magnet.
rows.note: Highest field produced (in part) by a superconductor; a DC test coil, not a user magnet; no journal paper found as of November 2026.

rows.description: Non-destructive pulsed magnet (generator-driven outsert + capacitor-driven insert), LANL
rows.citation: NHMFL Pulsed Field Facility, Los Alamos: 100.75 T multi-shot magnet, 22 March 2012 (LANL and US Department of Energy releases).
rows.note: User bore about 10 mm as operated (10 mm at 77 K, MagLab user page; 10.5 mm, IEEE Trans. Appl. Supercond., doi:10.1109/TASC.2023.3338580; the design figure was 15 mm). Outsert coils in a 225 mm bore driven by a 1.4 GW motor-generator supply 40-44 T and store 120 MJ; the insert (55-60 T, 1.4 MJ) is fired from a 2-2.2 MJ capacitor bank and takes the field from 40 T to 100 T in 8 ms; the field lasts about 15 ms inside an outsert pulse of 2.5-3 s, as often as once an hour (MagLab; Battesti et al., arXiv:1803.07547). Offline since 2019 while the generator rotor is replaced. No later record found (Toulouse 98.8 T, Dresden 95.6 T, Wuhan 94.8 T).

rows.description: Destructive single-turn coil (microsecond pulses)
rows.citation: ISSP Tokyo / LNCMI single-turn coil systems, of order 300 T (Herlach & Miura, High Magnetic Fields, 2003).

rows.description: Electromagnetic flux compression (destructive), ISSP Tokyo
rows.citation: Nakamura et al., Rev. Sci. Instrum. 89, 095106 (2018).

rows.description: Explosive-driven flux compression (destructive), VNIIEF
rows.citation: Boyko et al., Proc. 12th IEEE Int. Pulsed Power Conf., Monterey (1999), p. 746; reviewed in Boriskov et al., Phys.-Usp. 54, 421 (2011): about 28 MG.
rows.note: Year of the report; the date of the shot itself is not established in the sources consulted.

ladders.title: Pulsed energy stores
ladders.intro: The largest stores that deliver their energy in one pulse.

rows.description: Capacitor bank firing the insert coil of the LANL 100 T magnet
rows.citation: Battesti et al., arXiv:1803.07547 (2018): 2.2 MJ; National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, 'Meet the 100 tesla pulsed magnet': 2 MJ.

rows.description: Capacitor bank driving pulsed magnets, HZDR Dresden High Magnetic Field Lab
rows.citation: Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf publication records 13017 and 17042: 50 MJ modular capacitor bank, 24 kV maximum charging voltage, up to 500 kA and about 5 GW.

rows.description: Homopolar generator supply (6 x 10 MJ), UT Center for Electromechanics
rows.citation: UT-CEM Balcones homopolar generator power supply, 60 MJ, 1.5 MA at 600 V.

rows.description: Field energy of the outsert coils of the LANL 100 T magnet at full field (225 mm bore)
rows.citation: National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, 'Meet the 100 tesla pulsed magnet': stored magnetic energy at 100 T, 120 MJ in the outsert and 1.4 MJ in the insert.
rows.note: Charged over about a second by the 1.4 GW motor-generator, not by a capacitor bank.

rows.description: Capacitor bank energy, National Ignition Facility power conditioning system
rows.citation: LLNL National Ignition Facility power conditioning system (~400 MJ).

rows.description: Homopolar generator, Australian National University
rows.citation: ANU homopolar generator (1962-1986), 500 MJ stored rotational energy.

rows.description: Motor-generator rotational energy, NHMFL Pulsed Field Facility (1.4 GW)
rows.citation: LANL release (2012): a 1,200 MJ motor-generator powers the 100 T outsert; LANL's 2024 paper (doi:10.1109/TASC.2023.3338580) calls it a 1 GJ, 1.4 GW generator.
rows.note: Battesti et al. (arXiv:1803.07547) say the same 1.4 GW machine stores up to 600 MJ of rotational energy in a 300-ton shaft; the sources disagree by a factor of two.

thresholds.name: SC_FIELD_ESTABLISHED
thresholds.meaning: All-superconducting user magnets established (NHMFL, December 2017).

thresholds.name: SC_FIELD_RECORD
thresholds.meaning: All-superconducting record (CAS SECUF, January 2026, reported).

thresholds.name: SC_CONDUCTOR_RECORD
thresholds.meaning: Highest field at which a superconducting coil has operated, inside a resistive background (NHMFL Little Big Coil 9, August 2025, reported; the peer-reviewed predecessor is 45.5 T, Hahn et al. 2019).

thresholds.name: PULSED_NONDESTRUCTIVE_RECORD
thresholds.meaning: Non-destructive pulsed record (LANL, 22 March 2012, about 10 mm bore).

thresholds.name: PULSED_NONDESTRUCTIVE_BORE
thresholds.meaning: User bore of the 100 T LANL magnet as operated (10 mm at 77 K per the MagLab user page; 10.5 mm in LANL's 2024 paper; the design figure, still quoted on MagLab's overview page, was 15 mm).

thresholds.name: PULSED_ROUTINE_FIELD
thresholds.meaning: Field class of routine non-destructive pulsed user magnets (many laboratories run 60-75 T).

thresholds.name: PULSED_ROUTINE_BORE
thresholds.meaning: Largest bore treated as routine for that class (10-20 mm is typical; judgement).

thresholds.name: PULSED_RECORD_INSERT_BANK
thresholds.meaning: Capacitor bank that fires the insert coil of the LANL 100 T magnet (2 MJ per MagLab; 2.2 MJ per Battesti et al., arXiv:1803.07547).

thresholds.name: PULSED_RECORD_GENERATOR_POWER
thresholds.meaning: Motor-generator that drives the outsert coils of the LANL 100 T magnet for 2.5-3 s.

thresholds.name: PULSED_RECORD_OUTSERT_ENERGY
thresholds.meaning: Magnetic energy stored in the outsert coils of the LANL 100 T magnet at full field (MagLab); the insert stores 1.4 MJ.

thresholds.name: EMF_CONVENTIONAL_FIELD
thresholds.meaning: Field range of conventional industrial electromagnetic (magnetic-pulse) forming coils.

thresholds.name: SC_RAMP_RATE_SOTA
thresholds.meaning: Fastest routinely operated superconducting magnet ramps.

thresholds.name: SC_RAMP_RATE_EXTRAPOLATION
thresholds.meaning: Boundary beyond which pulsed superconducting operation is treated as aspirational (order-of-magnitude judgement; small HTS test coils; confidence estimated).

thresholds.name: ENERGY_MAGNET_DRIVER_SOTA
thresholds.meaning: Largest capacitor bank built as a pulsed-magnet driver (HZDR).

thresholds.name: ENERGY_ANY_STORE_RECORD
thresholds.meaning: Largest pulsed rotating store in a magnet facility (LANL motor-generator).

thresholds.name: PULSED_CURRENT_SOTA
thresholds.meaning: Peak currents routinely delivered by large capacitor-bank facilities to a single load.

thresholds.name: PULSED_CURRENT_RECORD
thresholds.meaning: Z machine peak load current.

thresholds.name: PEAK_POWER_SOTA
thresholds.meaning: Order of magnitude of the peak electrical power of the largest capacitor-bank installations (hundreds of megajoules released in under a millisecond; an estimated boundary). Pulsed-magnet banks are far below it: the 50 MJ Dresden bank delivers about 5 GW.

thresholds.name: PEAK_POWER_RECORD
thresholds.meaning: Sandia Z machine electrical power (~80 TW).

thresholds.name: SC_VOLTAGE_SOTA
thresholds.meaning: Upper end of terminal/quench-protection voltages of large superconducting magnets (ITER-class coils are designed for a few kV inside the cryostat).

thresholds.name: SC_VOLTAGE_EXTRAPOLATION
thresholds.meaning: Beyond this, insulation inside a cryostat is treated as aspirational (estimated boundary).

thresholds.name: PULSED_VOLTAGE_SOTA
thresholds.meaning: Capacitor-bank charging voltages of pulsed-magnet facilities (LANL/HZDR 10-24 kV).

thresholds.name: PULSED_VOLTAGE_EXTRAPOLATION
thresholds.meaning: Marx-generator class; beyond this, coil insulation is aspirational (estimated boundary).

thresholds.name: TNT_ENERGY_DENSITY
thresholds.meaning: Detonation energy of TNT per unit volume (4.184 MJ/kg x 1654 kg/m³), for scale.
